examples.ko: 그는 돌부리에 걸려 넘어져서 무릎을 다쳤어요.
examples.en: He tripped on a jagged stone and hurt his knee.
There are lots of jagged stones on the road, so walk carefully.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 돌부리를 힘껏 걷어찼어요.
examples.en: The child got angry and kicked a stone as hard as he could.

examples.ko: 산길을 걷다가 돌부리 때문에 발목을 삐었어요.
examples.en: While walking on the mountain path, I sprained my ankle because of a stone.
I kicked a stone and my shoe came off.
I dug out the protruding stones from the field one by one.

explain: '돌멩이'는 돌 하나를 가리키지만, '돌부리'는 땅에 박혀 위로 튀어나온 돌의 끝부분을 말해요. 보통 '돌부리에 걸리다', '돌부리에 채이다'처럼 걷다가 발이 걸리는 상황에서 말해요.
explain_en: '돌멩이' means a single stone, but '돌부리' is the tip of a stone stuck in the ground and sticking up. It is usually used in situations like '돌부리에 걸리다' or '돌부리에 채이다', where your foot catches on it as you walk.

examples.ko: 돌연사 위험을 줄이려면 정기 검진을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To lower the risk of sudden death, you should get regular checkups.

examples.ko: 과로가 돌연사의 원인이 될 수도 있대요.
examples.en: I heard overwork can also cause sudden death.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 젊은 사람의 돌연사 소식을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news on TV about the sudden death of a young person.
I get a health checkup every year to prevent sudden death.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 돌연사에 팬들이 큰 충격을 받았어요.
examples.en: The singer's sudden death shocked his fans deeply.

examples.ko: 심장이 약한 사람은 돌연사를 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: People with a weak heart need to be more careful about sudden death.

explain: 사고로 죽는 '사고사'와 달리, 겉으로는 건강해 보이던 사람이 갑자기 세상을 떠나는 경우에 써요. 건강 정보나 뉴스에서 '돌연사 예방', '돌연사 위험'처럼 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Unlike '사고사' (death by accident), it is used when someone who seemed healthy suddenly passes away. You hear it in health information and news in phrases like '돌연사 예방' (preventing sudden death) and '돌연사 위험' (risk of sudden death).

examples.ko: 그가 돌연히 회의 중에 일어나서 나갔어요.
examples.en: He suddenly got up and left in the middle of the meeting.

examples.ko: 돌연히 비가 쏟아져서 모두 뛰어 들어갔어요.
examples.en: It suddenly poured, so everyone ran inside.
My friend abruptly cut off contact, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 방 안의 불이 돌연히 꺼져서 깜깜해졌어요.
examples.en: The lights in the room suddenly went out and it became pitch dark.
That player abruptly announced his retirement.
The child suddenly burst into tears, and I was flustered.

explain: '갑자기'와 뜻은 같지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '갑자기'를 쓰는 게 자연스럽고, '돌연'처럼 '히' 없이도 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '갑자기' but sounds more formal, so it suits news and writing. In everyday conversation '갑자기' is more natural, and you can also say '돌연' without '히'.

examples.en: At the doljabi, our baby picked up the pencil.

examples.ko: 돌잡이 상에 실, 돈, 연필을 올려놓았어요.
examples.en: We put thread, money and a pencil on the doljabi table.

examples.ko: 돌잡이로 아이의 미래를 상상해 보며 웃었어요.
examples.en: We laughed as we imagined the child's future through the doljabi.
I heard that during the doljabi, the baby grabbed the microphone.

examples.ko: 요즘은 돌잡이 물건에 청진기나 골프공도 넣어요.
examples.en: These days people also put stethoscopes or golf balls among the doljabi items.

examples.ko: 제가 돌잡이 때 뭘 잡았는지 부모님께 여쭤봤어요.
examples.en: I asked my parents what I picked up at my doljabi.

explain: 아기의 첫 생일 잔치인 '돌잔치'에서 하는 순서 중 하나예요. 잔치 전체는 '돌잔치'라고 하고, 물건을 집게 하는 것을 '돌잡이를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is one part of the '돌잔치', the baby's first birthday party. The whole party is called '돌잔치', and having the baby pick an object is called '돌잡이를 하다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 돌팔이 의사라서 믿으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: He's a quack doctor, so you shouldn't trust him.
I got fooled by a quack and just wasted my money.

examples.ko: 자격증도 없이 돌팔이처럼 진료하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't treat patients like a quack without a license.

examples.ko: 인터넷에는 돌팔이 건강 정보가 너무 많아요.
examples.en: There is far too much quack health information on the internet.

examples.ko: 그 수리 기사는 돌팔이였는지 고장이 더 심해졌어요.
examples.en: That repairman must have been a quack, because it broke down even worse.
Please don't treat me like a quack.

explain: 주로 실력 없는 의사를 놀릴 때 쓰지만, 수리 기사나 상담가처럼 실력이 부족한 전문가에게도 써요. 상대를 깎아내리는 말이라서 사람 앞에서 직접 말하면 크게 실례예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for an incompetent doctor, but also for other under-skilled professionals such as repairmen or counselors. It is a put-down, so saying it to someone's face is very rude.

examples.ko: 우리는 오랜 동고동락 끝에 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: After a long time of sharing hard times and good, we opened a small shop.
The bond from sharing joys and sorrows is not easily forgotten.

examples.ko: 그와의 동고동락이 제 인생의 큰 힘이었어요.
examples.en: The time I shared through thick and thin with him was a great strength in my life.

examples.ko: 삼 년간의 동고동락을 마치고 우리는 헤어졌어요.
examples.en: After three years of living through everything together, we parted ways.

examples.ko: 동고동락하는 사이라서 말 안 해도 서로 알아요.
examples.en: We share everything, so we understand each other without words.
The longer the time you've shared through good and bad, the deeper the affection.

explain: 오래 함께 지낸 가족, 동료, 팀처럼 정이 깊은 사이를 말할 때 어울려요. 짧게 만난 사이에는 잘 안 쓰고, '동고동락하다' 형태로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It fits close relationships built over a long time, such as family, coworkers or a team. It is not used for people you have only just met, and it is often said in the form '동고동락하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 동료들과 동고동락했어요.
examples.en: I shared the ups and downs with my coworkers for ten years.
I met a friend after a long time who I went through army life with.
We lived through everything together like family, so our bond is very deep.
The coach built the team by sharing everything with the players.
It is an honor to share life's ups and downs with him.
I feel sad to part with the staff I went through so much with.

explain: 기쁜 일도 힘든 일도 같이 겪으며 지낸다는 느낌이라, 보통 '함께', '~와/과'와 같이 써요. 말할 때는 '같이 고생하면서 지냈다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of going through both happy and hard times together, so it usually appears with '함께' or '~와/과'. In speech people may also say it in plain words like '같이 고생하면서 지냈다'.

examples.en: The baby's face is slightly round, so it's really cute.
This stone is roundish in shape and smooth.
Roundish glasses suit your face well.
I roll the dough so that the bread comes out roundish.
It's a night when the moon looks nearly round.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 제 얼굴이 더 동그스름했어요.
examples.en: My face was rounder when I was little.

explain: '동그랗다'가 또렷한 원 모양이라면, '동그스름하다'는 '조금 동그란 듯하다'는 느낌이에요. 얼굴, 돌, 안경테처럼 완전한 원은 아니지만 부드럽게 둥근 모양에 많이 써요. '둥그스름하다'는 같은 모양을 조금 더 큰 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: While '동그랗다' means a clear circle, '동그스름하다' feels like 'somewhat round'. It suits softly rounded shapes that are not perfect circles, such as faces, stones or glasses frames. '둥그스름하다' describes the same kind of shape but with a slightly bigger feel.

examples.en: Parents are happy when siblings get along well.

examples.ko: 저는 동기간에 사이가 좋아서 외롭지 않았어요.
examples.en: My siblings and I got along well, so I was never lonely.

examples.ko: 동기간끼리 돈 문제로 다투면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts when siblings fight over money.
The bond between siblings grows deeper as you get older.
Even among siblings, you should respect each other.

examples.ko: 명절에는 동기간 모두 모여서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: On holidays, all the siblings gather and eat together.

explain: 형제자매 사이를 가리키는 말로, 주로 어른들의 말이나 글에서 들려요. 회사나 학교에서 같은 때에 들어온 사람을 뜻하는 '동기'와는 한자도 뜻도 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to the relationship among brothers and sisters and is mostly heard from older people or in writing. It is different from '동기', which means people who joined a company or school at the same time.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 빵은 오전에 벌써 동나요.
examples.en: The popular bread has already run out by the morning.

examples.ko: 마스크가 동나서 약국을 여러 군데 돌았어요.
examples.en: Masks were sold out, so I went around to several pharmacies.
My allowance has already run out.
I heard the concert tickets sold out in an instant.
When the ingredients run out, we close early.

examples.ko: 물건이 다 동날 때까지 세일을 해요.
examples.en: They have the sale until everything is gone.

explain: '떨어지다'는 조금 모자라게 된 때도 쓰지만, '동나다'는 가게의 물건이나 재고가 하나도 남지 않았을 때 잘 써요. '표가 동나다', '재료가 동나다'처럼 팔리거나 써서 바닥난 경우에 어울려요.
explain_en: '떨어지다' can also be used when something is merely running short, but '동나다' fits stock that has completely run out, such as goods in a shop. It suits things that sold out or got used up, as in '표가 동나다' or '재료가 동나다'.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 스님이 마을을 돌며 동냥을 했대요.
examples.en: They say that in the old days monks went around villages to beg.
I heard he barely got by on what he begged for.

examples.ko: 문 앞에 동냥 온 사람에게 밥을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: I shared a meal with the person who came to the door to beg.

examples.ko: 동냥 그릇에 동전 몇 개가 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: There were a few coins in the begging bowl.
I heard they cooked rice with the rice they begged for.
She said she would beg if she had to in order to feed her child.

explain: '구걸'과 비슷하지만 '동냥'은 옛이야기나 스님이 쌀과 돈을 얻으러 다니는 모습처럼 옛날 느낌이 있어요. '귀동냥'처럼 다른 말과 합쳐서도 써요.

phrases.en: I picked it up by overhearing the conversation at the next seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식으로 배우거나 직접 듣지 않고 곁에서 들어서 알게 된다는 뜻이에요. '귀동냥으로 배우다'처럼 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means getting to know something by overhearing, not by learning or being told formally. It is often used as '귀동냥으로 배우다'.

explain_en: It is similar to '구걸' (begging), but '동냥' has an old-fashioned feel, as in old stories or monks going around to receive rice and money. It also appears in compounds like '귀동냥'.

examples.en: In the old days, people went house to house and begged for food.
A man is begging for money by the roadside.
I heard she fed her family by begging for rice.

examples.ko: 그 스님은 마을을 돌며 동냥하는 것이 수행이었어요.
examples.en: For that monk, going around the village to beg was his practice.

examples.ko: 동냥하러 다니는 사람이 요즘은 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The number of people going around to beg has dropped a lot these days.
It was a time when there was nothing to eat even if you begged.

explain: 요즘 일상에서는 '구걸하다'가 더 일반적이고, '동냥하다'는 옛이야기나 스님이 얻으러 다니는 모습에 어울려요. 보통 '밥을 동냥하다', '쌀을 동냥하다'처럼 얻는 것을 앞에 써요.
explain_en: In daily speech '구걸하다' is more general, while '동냥하다' fits old stories or monks going around to receive food. The thing obtained usually comes before it, as in '밥을 동냥하다' or '쌀을 동냥하다'.

examples.en: Since I'm the youngest, I'm always the punching bag at home.
Because I'm new, everyone makes me their punching bag.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 이번 시즌 내내 동네북 신세였어요.
examples.en: That team was everyone's punching bag all season.

examples.ko: 왜 제가 항상 동네북이 되어야 해요?
examples.en: Why do I always have to be the punching bag?
I got a comment from every direction like a punching bag.
You can't treat someone as a doormat just because they're nice.

explain: 누구나 한 번씩 만만하게 건드리고 탓하는 사람을 말해요. '샌드백'과 비슷하게 들리지만, 동네북은 특히 여러 사람에게 두루 놀림이나 비난을 받는 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It refers to someone whom everyone feels free to pick on and blame. It sounds similar to 'punching bag', but '동네북' especially means a person who gets teased or criticized by many different people.

examples.en: The eastern sky slowly grew bright.
The sun is rising in the east.

examples.ko: 우리는 동녘이 트기 전에 산에 올랐어요.
examples.en: We climbed the mountain before the eastern sky began to lighten.
At dawn I opened the window facing east.
I made a wish while looking toward the east.

examples.ko: 동녘의 첫 햇살이 바다를 붉게 물들였어요.
examples.en: The first sunlight in the east dyed the sea red.

explain: '동쪽'과 같은 방향이지만 시나 글에서 많이 쓰고, 해가 뜨는 새벽 하늘 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '동쪽'이 자연스럽고, 반대는 '서녘'이에요.
explain_en: It points to the same direction as '동쪽', but is common in poems and writing and carries the feel of the dawn sky where the sun rises. In daily conversation '동쪽' is more natural, and the opposite is '서녘'.

examples.en: I got angry and hurled my bag onto the floor.

examples.ko: 그는 들고 있던 책을 동댕이치고 나가 버렸어요.
examples.en: He flung down the book he was holding and walked out.
If you hurl your phone, it will break.
The child threw the toy down and it broke.
He dropped his luggage as if throwing it and left.
Please don't throw things like that.

explain: '던지다'는 보통 던지는 행동 자체를 말하지만, '동댕이치다'는 화가 나거나 거칠게 힘을 줘서 내던지는 느낌이 있어요. '내동댕이치다'라고도 말하는데 뜻이 같아요.
explain_en: '던지다' usually just describes the act of throwing, but '동댕이치다' has the feel of flinging something roughly, often out of anger. You can also say '내동댕이치다' with the same meaning.

examples.en: I was in a hurry, so I waited stamping my feet.
The child is hopping from foot to foot, probably needing the bathroom.
The road was jammed, so I stamped my feet in frustration.
I stamped my feet from the cold and then went into the shop.
Mom was anxiously fidgeting while waiting for the exam results.

examples.ko: 동동거려 봐야 버스는 빨리 안 와요.
examples.en: Stamping your feet won't make the bus come any faster.

explain: 안타깝거나 추워서 발을 자꾸 구르는 모습에 써요. 보통 '발을 동동거리다'라고 하고, 같은 모습을 '발을 동동 구르다'로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과를 기다리며 발을 동동 굴렀어요.
phrases.en: I was on pins and needles waiting for the exam results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 발을 구르지 않아도 마음이 급하고 안타까워 어쩔 줄 모를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use it even if you are not actually stamping, when you are so anxious or frustrated that you don't know what to do.
phrases.en_equiv: be on pins and needles; fret anxiously

explain_en: It describes someone repeatedly stamping their feet out of anxiety or cold. People usually say '발을 동동거리다', and the same scene is also commonly described as '발을 동동 구르다'.

examples.en: The child is excited and stamping their feet.
In my hurry, I fidgeted anxiously at the door.

examples.ko: 추운 날 버스를 기다리며 동동대고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was stamping my feet waiting for the bus on a cold day.
Even though I waited anxiously, there was no news.
Don't fidget like that. Sit down and wait.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마를 보고 다리를 동동대다가 웃었어요.
examples.en: The baby kicked its legs at seeing Mom and then laughed.

explain: '동동거리다'와 같은 뜻으로, 발을 자꾸 구르거나 안달하는 모습을 말해요. 일상에서는 '발을 동동 구르다'라는 표현으로 더 많이 들어요.
explain_en: It has the same meaning as '동동거리다', describing repeated foot-stamping or restless fretting. In daily speech you more often hear the expression '발을 동동 구르다'.

examples.en: I felt a sense of camaraderie in a difficult situation.
Our team has an exceptional bond among coworkers.
Thanks to the camaraderie, I got through even the hard overtime.

examples.ko: 동료애로 똘똘 뭉친 소방관들이 구조에 나섰어요.
examples.en: Firefighters united by comradeship set out on the rescue.

examples.ko: 진짜 동료애는 힘들 때 드러나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think true comradeship shows when times are hard.
They overcame the crisis through the power of deep comradeship.

explain: '우정'은 친구 사이의 정이고, '동료애'는 같은 직장이나 팀에서 같이 일하는 사람들 사이의 정이에요. 힘든 일을 함께 겪을 때 '동료애를 느끼다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '우정' is affection between friends, while '동료애' is the bond among people who work together in the same workplace or team. People often say '동료애를 느끼다' when going through hard work together.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 점수가 동률이라서 연장전에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The two teams' scores were tied, so it went into extra time.
The voting result came out as a tie.
When grades are tied, we decide by drawing lots.
Three people ended up tied for first place.
In the last game they broke the tie and won the title.

examples.ko: 동률인 팀끼리 한 번 더 겨뤄요.
examples.en: The teams that are tied play each other once more.

explain: '무승부'는 경기에서 비긴 결과를 말하고, '동률'은 점수, 표, 순위 같은 숫자가 똑같다는 점에 초점이 있어요. '동률 1위', '동률을 이루다'처럼 순위와 함께 많이 써요.
explain_en: '무승부' is the result of a game ending in a draw, while '동률' focuses on numbers such as scores, votes or rankings being equal. It is often used with rankings, as in '동률 1위' or '동률을 이루다'.

examples.en: He keeps giving irrelevant answers, maybe because he didn't hear the question.
I got nervous in the interview and ended up giving an off-topic answer.
I asked for directions and he answered something unrelated, which was absurd.

examples.ko: 동문서답하지 말고 제 질문에 대답해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't give an irrelevant answer; answer my question.
If you get asked a question while dozing off, it's easy to answer off the mark.

examples.ko: 그분은 귀가 잘 안 들려서 가끔 동문서답하세요.
examples.en: He doesn't hear well, so he sometimes answers off the topic.

explain: 질문과 상관없는 엉뚱한 대답을 할 때 써요. 일부러 딴소리를 할 때도, 잘못 알아들어서 그럴 때도 쓸 수 있어요. '동문서답을 하다', '동문서답이다'처럼 명사로도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone gives an answer that has nothing to do with the question, whether on purpose or from misunderstanding. It also works as a noun, as in '동문서답을 하다' or '동문서답이다'.

examples.en: He avoided danger with his animal instinct.

examples.ko: 동물적 본능 때문에 순간 몸이 움직였어요.
examples.en: My body moved in an instant because of animal instinct.

examples.ko: 그 요리사는 동물적 감각으로 간을 맞춰요.
examples.en: That chef seasons food by pure instinct.
His almost animal sense of smell is truly amazing.

examples.ko: 동물적 직감이 뛰어난 선수라서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: He is popular because he is a player with excellent instinct.
I felt primal fear in the dark alley.

explain: '동물적 감각', '동물적 본능'처럼 뒤에 명사가 와요. '동물적 감각'은 생각하기 전에 몸이 먼저 아는 뛰어난 직감을 칭찬하는 말이고, 문맥에 따라 거칠고 본능적이라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: A noun follows it, as in '동물적 감각' or '동물적 본능'. '동물적 감각' praises excellent intuition, where the body knows before you think, and depending on context it can also mean rough and instinctive.

examples.en: I heard Korea has been known since long ago as the land of courtesy in the East.

examples.ko: 어른께 인사도 안 하다니 동방예의지국이 맞나 싶어요.
examples.en: Not even greeting an elder, I wonder if this is really the 'land of courtesy'.
True to the 'land of courtesy', I offered the elder a seat first.
Foreigners find it interesting when they hear the term 'land of courtesy in the East'.

examples.ko: 요즘 동방예의지국의 예절이 많이 달라졌다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the manners of the 'land of courtesy' have changed a lot lately.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 동방예의지국 소리를 들은 게 자랑이라고 하세요.
examples.en: Grandfather says he is proud that Korea was called the 'land of courtesy'.

explain: 우리나라가 예의 바른 나라라고 불렸다는 오래된 자랑스러운 표현이에요. 요즘은 예의 없는 행동을 보고 '동방예의지국 맞아?'처럼 비꼬듯 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is an old, proud expression saying Korea was known as a courteous country. These days people also use it sarcastically when they see rude behavior, as in '동방예의지국 맞아?'.
